confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on two web searches. One confirmed the RBA rate. The other covered aggregated Munich cost-of-living data published around March to July 2026, mainly Numbeo figures quoted by Expatica, plus HousingAnywhere and MyLifeElsewhere. Typical values were about EUR 4.0 for a cappuccino, about EUR 5.2 for a 0.5 L draught beer, about EUR 18.7 for an inexpensive meal and about EUR 83 for a three-course meal for two. I converted these at about 1.10 USD per EUR, a rate implied by the RBA's AUD/USD and AUD/EUR mid-points for 18 November 2026. The cocktail (about EUR 12) and wine glass (about EUR 6.5) figures were not directly checked. They are estimated from the local price level relative to beer and are less certain. All accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July. Munich's peak summer season and big events can push hotel rates higher, so the hotel and hostel figures are the least certain. A third-party summary of the RBA page also reported the 18 November 2026 observation at 0.6720.
comparable_city_reasoning: Munich is one of Germany's most expensive cities. It is broadly comparable to Frankfurt and Zurich-adjacent price levels and pricier than Berlin, especially for accommodation in the summer peak.
